reasoning:
The claim that the Great Wall of China is visible from space (and specifically that it is the "only" such structure) is a well-documented myth that has been thoroughly debunked by NASA, astronauts, and optical physics. 

Because the Great Wall is relatively narrow (averaging only 5 to 9 meters in width) and constructed from materials that match the color of the surrounding soil and mountains, it is virtually impossible to see from low Earth orbit with the naked eye. China's own astronaut, Yang Liwei, confirmed after his 2003 mission that he was unable to see the wall. 

Conversely, many other man-made structures—such as major highways, airport runways, large dams, the pyramids of Giza (under perfect conditions), and cities illuminated at night—are visible from space to the naked eye. Therefore, the Great Wall is neither visible from space with the naked eye, nor is it the "only" man-made structure that could be seen.
